title: an external project's later round brings its branch up to date with the base by a merge, never a rewrite: fm-worker merges origin/<base> into the task branch before the agent starts, hands any conflicting files to the worker by name, commits the merge with the round and pushes it fast-forward, and gate 2 accepts an external branch that already contains its base
acceptance: Why. 2026-10-06 ~01:45, agent-wardrobe (external project maker-founder, base master) PR #1 (branch t-002-work, head 1f038ee, review round 2 APPROVED) became CONFLICTING after the captain pushed 8a4f393 and 1601a1e to master; a trial rebase stops on main.cjs and styles.css, and `bin/fm-gate.sh` gate 2 ('rebases onto 1601a1e cleanly') is red. Round 3 was briefed to merge master in, and the worker answered WORKER_BLOCKED / ASK-MERGE-PREPARATION: the round's sandbox cannot write git history, and fm-worker.sh's `bring_up_to_date` (bin/fm-worker.sh:1059-1063) returns at once for `FM_EXTERNAL=1` with 'external rewrites require the explicit restack helper and expected-head lease'. Its self path rebuilds by squash onto the base and force-pushes with a lease (bin/fm-worker.sh:1065-1144, :2112-2142), which an external project must never do (the publish path already refuses it at :2120-2123 with exit 65; tests/onboarding-crew.test.sh:152-160). So nothing in the engine can bring an external branch up to date with its base, and every external PR whose base moves into a conflict is stuck. The autopilot's GitHub update-branch (bin/lib/fm_autopilot_branches.py:131-175) only works for a BEHIND PR, never a conflicting one.

Mechanism. External branches are never rewritten (no rebase, no squash rebuild, no force-push; design §15). The only non-rewriting way to take the base's change into the branch is a merge commit on top of the branch head, pushed fast-forward. And gate 2 (bin/fm-gate.sh:184-201) asks `git rebase $BASE` in a scratch worktree, which linearises a branch that holds such a merge commit, replays the branch's own commits onto the base and stops on the very conflict the merge resolved, so even a correct catch-up stays red at gate 2 for an external project.

Change 1, fm-worker.sh: a new function `external_catch_up` (defined beside `bring_up_to_date`; the self body of `bring_up_to_date` is unchanged), called from the FM_EXTERNAL=1 branch of `bring_up_to_date` in place of the early-return message (so the existing call at bin/fm-worker.sh:1146, `if [ "$round_two" = 1 ]; then bring_up_to_date; fi`, reaches it for external later rounds). It runs before the agent starts and before `mirror_sync`. Steps, each failure saying why in en and zh-TW on stderr: (a0) only when the project's confirmed merge method is `squash` or `merge`: read it with `fm_stack_policy merge_method` (bin/lib/fm-stack.sh:29-30, already sourced by fm-worker.sh at :20 and used by bin/fm-merge.sh:66); under `rebase` GitHub's rebase landing replays the branch's own commits and drops the merge commit, so a catch-up cannot help and would let gate 2 pass a branch that cannot land: it says 'the project lands by rebase; <branch> is not caught up by a merge' and returns 0 without merging, and an unreadable policy refuses with exit 65; (a) only with an open PR (`$PR` set): with no PR it says the branch is not caught up this round and returns 0; (b) the worktree must be clean (`git status --porcelain` empty) or it says so and returns 0 without merging, as the self path does at :1066-1071; (c) the expected-head lease: the head the round was bound to is the output of the existing external `fm_binding head --task "$TASK" --pr "$PR" --branch "$branch"` call at bin/fm-worker.sh:631 (it already verifies that the PR head, the fetched refs/pull/<n>/head and the local task ref agree), now captured into a variable (for example `bound_head`) instead of discarded to /dev/null, with its `|| exit 65` kept; `external_catch_up` reads `git ls-remote --exit-code --heads origin refs/heads/$branch` and `git -C "$tree" rev-parse HEAD`, and when either differs from the bound head it refuses with exit 65 ('origin's <branch> is not the head this round was bound to; not merging <base> into it') before any merge; (d) fetch the base with `git fetch -q origin +refs/heads/$BASE:refs/remotes/origin/$BASE` (as :1072); a failed fetch says so and returns 0 without merging; (e) if `git merge-base --is-ancestor refs/remotes/origin/$BASE HEAD` the branch already contains the base: nothing to do, return 0; (f) otherwise record `caught_up=1`, `catchup_prev` (the bound head) and `catchup_base` (the fetched base sha), then run in the worktree, attached on the task branch, `git -c merge.conflictStyle=merge -c rerere.enabled=false merge --no-ff --no-commit -q refs/remotes/origin/$BASE`. Never `rebase`, never `checkout --detach`, never `reset` the branch, never `push --force` or `--force-with-lease`. A merge that fails without leaving an unmerged path runs `git merge --abort` and exits 70 before any worker starts ('could not merge <base> into <branch>'). The merge is left in progress (MERGE_HEAD set) whether it applied cleanly or not, and is concluded by the round's normal commit below. The conflict lists are collected exactly as the rebuild collects them, into the same arrays `rebuild_conflicts`, `rebuild_bare`, `rebuild_bare_left`, `rebuild_bare_side` (move the collection loops at :1122-1135 into one helper both paths call, behaviour unchanged for the self path). The side wording takes the merge direction: in a rebuild git's stage 2 ('ours') is the base and stage 3 ('theirs') the task (the worktree is detached at the base and the task squash-merged onto it, :1103-1105); in a catch-up the task branch is checked out and the base merged in, so stage 2 is the task and stage 3 the base. `rebuild_side_left` (:954-969) takes the direction as a second argument (for example `rebuild_side_left <path> [catchup]`) and swaps which stage it calls the base's and which the task's, so every sentence it prints names the right side in both paths; the rebuild's calls and wording are unchanged; `rebuild_own_file_restore` and `rebuild_lost` are not run for an external project, whose task file is private and never in the tree (the guard at :1118 already keeps `fm_task` from being read for FM_EXTERNAL=1). `rebuild_mark` is taken with `rebuild_fingerprint` (it reads over `${rebuild_base:-HEAD}`, and HEAD stays the bound head during a merge, so `rebuild_base` is left empty for a catch-up). It emits `emit_status "Merged $BASE into $branch" "已把 $BASE 合併進 $branch"`.

Change 2, the worker prompt (the block that prints '# Your branch was rebuilt on the current' at bin/fm-worker.sh:1322-1374): when `caught_up=1` it prints instead a section '# The current <BASE> was merged into your branch' saying: <BASE> moved and the branch did not contain it, so fm-worker.sh merged origin/<BASE> (<catchup_base>) into the branch at <catchup_prev>; the merge is in progress, not committed, and fm-worker.sh commits it with this round as one merge commit; the conflicting files with markers and the files without markers (with which side the worktree holds) listed exactly as the rebuild section lists them, with the same resolve rule (keep BOTH sides: the base's change and the task's intent; never take a whole side); with no conflicts, 'Every file merged cleanly; there is nothing to resolve.'; and: do not commit, abort or restart the merge, and do not run git history commands — a round whose HEAD is no longer <catchup_prev> on the branch, or whose merge is no longer in progress, is refused. The rebuilt section's task-file sentences are not printed for a catch-up.

Change 3, the round's work and publication. `worker_changed_files` (:1398) compares `rebuild_fingerprint` with `rebuild_mark` when `caught_up=1`, as it does for `rebuilt=1`. `rebuild_publishes` (:1434) is true also for `caught_up=1` with nothing unresolved (`rebuild_unresolved` false), so a clean catch-up is committed and pushed whatever the worker did (changed files, nothing, a note, or only asked), at every place that reads it (:1826, :1828, :1866, the asked/refused block at :1880-1922 — whose `elif [ "$rebuilt" = 1 ]` at :1883 also applies to `caught_up=1` — and the 'changed nothing' exit at :1928, whose condition becomes `[ "$rebuilt" = 0 ] && [ "$caught_up" = 0 ] && ...` or reads `rebuild_publishes`); an unresolved catch-up the worker did not touch publishes nothing and is not 'the adapter changed nothing' noise beyond what an unresolved rebuild already says. `publish_wip_if_dirty` (:227-281) treats an uncommitted catch-up like an uncommitted rebuild: it says 'the merge of <base> into <branch> was not committed (<reason>); nothing is published' and publishes nothing (a half-resolved merge with markers is never a checkpoint); the next round finds the dirty tree and rescues it as today. `post_note` (bin/fm-worker.sh:1648-1665) projects the worker stage early for an external non-`comments` projection when `! worker_changed_files` (:1655); that condition becomes `! worker_changed_files && ! rebuild_publishes`, so a clean catch-up (always published) is projected once, after publication at its merge-commit head (:2236-2241), never first at `catchup_prev`.

Change 4, the checks before the commit, beside the rebuilt ones at :1958-2050 and through the same refusal (`rebuild_refuse`, exit 75, whose message names the branch staying at <catchup_prev>): when `caught_up=1`, refuse if HEAD is not attached on `$branch` at `catchup_prev`, or if `git rev-parse -q --verify MERGE_HEAD` is not `catchup_base` (the worker aborted, committed or restarted the merge); then the same conflict-marker scan over every file the commit carries, read from the index against `catchup_base` (`git diff --cached --name-only -z --diff-filter=d "$catchup_base"`: the task's whole change plus every file the worker resolved, exactly the set the rebuild scans against `rebuild_base` at :1975-1976; never against `catchup_prev`, which would also read every file the base changed, so a base file holding a literal `<<<<<<< ` line would refuse every round), and the same 'conflicts with no markers still exactly as the merge left them' check. `new_scripts_executable` reads against `catchup_base` and `catchup_prev` as it does for a rebuild (:2054-2056). The commit is NOT made with `git commit` (which would move `refs/heads/<branch>` at once and open a window where a kill leaves the local branch on an unrecorded, unpushed merge). As the rebuild does (:2075-2111, the identity rule, the gpgSign read and `commit-tree`), it writes the index tree and builds the merge commit with `git commit-tree <tree> -p "$catchup_prev" -p "$catchup_base" -m "$commit_msg"`, so its parents are exactly (catchup_prev, catchup_base) by construction; it records it at `refs/fm-caughtup/<branch>` first; only then moves the local branch with a compare-and-swap `git update-ref refs/heads/$branch <merge commit> "$catchup_prev"` and ends the merge state with `git merge --quit` (index and worktree already hold the merge commit's tree, so the worktree is clean); a failure in any of these exits 70 with nothing pushed and, if the branch already moved, moves it back by compare-and-swap. A kill at any point before the branch move leaves the branch at `catchup_prev`; after it, `refs/fm-caughtup/<branch>` exists for `catchup_settle`. The push is the existing plain fast-forward push after `fm_publication_policy` (:2144-2146), never forced: origin refuses it if the branch moved, which exits 71 as today. The pushed event carries `--data '{"caught_up":{"previous_head":…,"base":…,"base_head":…,"head":…,"conflicts":[…]}}'`, built like `rebuild_args` (:2153-2158); no PR comment is posted for an external catch-up (external projections are policy-governed, :2236-2241). For a catch-up `fm_publication_policy "$tree"` (today at :2144, after the commit) is run before the commit, so a policy refusal (65) leaves no unpushed merge commit; the existing call after the commit stays for every other round. Recovery: on a refused push (71) the local task branch is moved back to `catchup_prev` with a compare-and-swap `git update-ref refs/heads/$branch $catchup_prev <merge commit>` (local ref only; origin is never touched), then deletes `refs/fm-caughtup/<branch>` itself, and the message names the merge commit by its id (as the rebuild's refused push does at :2129-2131), never a ref that the exit-path settle would remove, so the next round's `fm_binding head` (:631) finds the local ref equal to the PR head again instead of exiting 65 forever; the worktree is left for the next round's rescue as today. After a successful push `refs/fm-caughtup/<branch>` is deleted. This is a local-ref move under compare-and-swap, not a rewrite of the published branch. A run cut short after the commit and before the push (a signal between :2100 and :2146, when `_fm_wip_done=1` already silences the exit trap) is settled at the next round's start by a new `catchup_settle`, called beside every `rebuild_settle` call (:324 in the exit path and :594 before the branch fetch at :597): when `refs/fm-caughtup/<branch>` exists it asks origin (`git ls-remote --heads origin refs/heads/<branch>`, fetching that head when it is not local, as `rebuild_settle` does at :291-322). If origin's head contains the merge commit (equal to it or a descendant, `git merge-base --is-ancestor`, as `rebuild_settle` counts one at :302-303), it keeps the local branch and deletes the ref. In every other case (origin still at the first parent, origin moved to some other commit — for example the captain pushed to the PR branch — or the branch absent on origin): if the local branch is the merge commit it moves the local branch back to the merge commit's first parent with a compare-and-swap `update-ref` (so the next round's non-forced fetch at :597 and `fm_binding head` at :631 meet origin's head as they would without the catch-up, and a moved origin is refused there as it is today, not left stuck on an unpublished merge), and it deletes the ref; after the 71 path the ref is already gone, so the exit-path settle finds nothing to do. The ref is deleted in every case except when origin cannot be asked: then it says so and leaves both for the next round (return 1, as `rebuild_settle` does). So `fm_binding head` (:631) never meets a local ref ahead of the PR head left by a catch-up.

Change 6, bin/fm-checkpoint.sh: it refuses (exit 71, the code it already uses for a refused branch, with 'fm-checkpoint: a merge is in progress on <branch>; fm-worker.sh commits it' in en and zh-TW) when the tree has a merge in progress (`git -C "$tree" rev-parse -q --verify MERGE_HEAD` succeeds), checked right after the protected-branch guard at bin/fm-checkpoint.sh:88-101 and before any `add -A` or commit (:103-110). A rebuild is safe from it only because its worktree is detached (bin/fm-worker.sh:935-938); a catch-up stays attached with the merge in progress, so without this a mid-round checkpoint from outside the sandbox would conclude and push a merge that still has conflict markers. skills/worker/SKILL.md 'When the base moved under your branch' (:98-119) is edited in place: on an external project the later round instead merges the base into your branch and leaves the merge in progress; resolve the listed files under the same rules; do not commit, abort or restart the merge; fm-checkpoint.sh refuses while the merge is in progress and fm-worker.sh commits and pushes it.

Change 5, gate 2 (bin/fm-gate.sh:184-201): for `FM_EXTERNAL=1` only, and only when the project's merge method (`fm_stack_policy merge_method`; fm-gate.sh already sources bin/lib/fm-stack.sh at :82-83) is `squash` or `merge`, when `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$BASE" "$BRANCH"` (the branch already contains the base tip, as after a catch-up or a GitHub update-branch), gate 2 passes without the rebase replay — a squash merge of such a branch onto that base is the branch's own tree, so it cannot conflict. Under `rebase` (bin/lib/fm_conventions.py:10; the autopilot lands with it at bin/lib/fm_autopilot.py:622) the replay always runs, because GitHub's rebase landing replays the branch's own commits. Otherwise the existing replay runs unchanged. Self projects keep the replay exactly as it is.

Exit codes and messages: no new code. 65 gains 'an external branch that is not the head the round was bound to' (already the bucket for 'an unverifiable external PR head'); 70 gains 'a merge of the base into an external branch that could not be made'; 75 gains 'a caught-up external round whose merge was aborted or committed in the round, whose HEAD left the bound head, or that left a conflict marker or an unmarked conflict as the merge left it'. design/design.md's exit-code paragraph (§5.3.2, the sentence at design.md:897-915 that tests/worker-exits.test.sh:215-240 compares (it compares the set of codes only, so it keeps passing with no new code)) is edited in place to say so.

Tests (fail-first; workers do not run suites; CI and the gates verify; fail-first runs only *.test.sh). New bash suite tests/worker-external-catchup.test.sh in the style of tests/external-execution.test.sh (python unittest inside bash, using tests/lib/crew_blocks.py `function`/`section`/`shell`, no network: a local bare repository is `origin`). Cases, each its own assertion: (1) a branch whose base moved without conflict: `external_catch_up` leaves MERGE_HEAD = the new base, HEAD still the branch head attached on the branch, empty conflict list, and no `rebase`, `reset`, `checkout --detach` or `push` among the git calls (record them with a wrapper); (2) a conflicting base: the conflicting file is in `rebuild_conflicts` with markers in the worktree; (3) the lease: origin's branch head differs from the bound head → exit 65 and no merge started (no MERGE_HEAD); (4) the base already an ancestor → returns 0, no MERGE_HEAD; (5) the pre-commit block with `caught_up=1` refuses (exit 75) when MERGE_HEAD is gone and when a marker remains, and passes when resolved, after which the commit has parents (catchup_prev, catchup_base), `refs/fm-caughtup/<branch>` was written before `refs/heads/<branch>` moved, and MERGE_HEAD is gone with a clean worktree; (6) gate 2 from bin/fm-gate.sh with FM_EXTERNAL=1 on a branch that merged its base after a conflict returns 0, and with FM_EXTERNAL=0 still runs the replay. (7) bin/fm-checkpoint.sh run with --dir on a tree with a merge in progress exits 71 and makes no commit (no new commit on the branch, MERGE_HEAD still set). (8) a catch-up conflict without markers (one side deletes a file the other changes): `rebuild_bare_side` names the task's version as the task's and the base's as the base's, and the same case through the rebuild keeps today's wording; (9) with merge method `rebase` in the conventions, `external_catch_up` starts no merge and gate 2 with FM_EXTERNAL=1 on a branch containing its base still runs the replay (returns non-zero on the conflicting fixture); (10) a refused push (origin moved) after a catch-up commit, run through the exit trap (`finished`), leaves `refs/heads/<branch>` back at `catchup_prev`, no `refs/fm-caughtup/<branch>`, and the merge commit's id in the message; (10b) `post_note` with FM_EXTERNAL=1, a non-comments projection and a clean catch-up (`rebuild_publishes` true, no worker change) makes no early projection. (11) a base file that holds a literal `<<<<<<< ` line at the start of a line, merged cleanly by the catch-up, does not refuse the commit; (12) an interrupted round (merge commit made, `refs/fm-caughtup/<branch>` set, push never ran, origin still at `catchup_prev`): `catchup_settle` moves the local branch back to `catchup_prev` and deletes the ref; with origin already at the merge commit, or at a descendant of it, it keeps the branch and deletes the ref; with origin at an unrelated commit it moves the local branch back to `catchup_prev` and deletes the ref;  with origin unreachable it returns 1 and keeps both. Cases 1-12 fail on base (no `external_catch_up`; gate 2 replays and stops). tests/onboarding-crew.test.sh:152-160 `test_external_rebuild_is_held_and_never_reads_public_spec` is changed in place: its first half (no git call at all from `bring_up_to_date` for an external project) becomes 'no rebase, squash rebuild, reset or force-push, and no `fm_task` read'; its second half (the rebuilt publish path still exits 65 for FM_EXTERNAL=1 without a push) stays. tests/worker-rebuild.test.sh and tests/lib/worker-rebuild.sh (self rebuild) keep passing unchanged; if moving the conflict collection into a helper changes any string they assert, update that string only. Existing tests that extract or stub the blocks this task changes keep passing, with their section anchors kept intact (or the tests updated in place in the same commit): tests/onboarding-crew.test.sh:107, :156-160, :164, :168 and :174-175 (`test_final_push_is_gated_before_git`, the `'_fm_wip_done=1\nif [ "$rebuilt" = 1 ]; then'` … `'# Only now: a push'` section), tests/conventions-publication.test.sh:55 (`publish_wip_if_dirty` run with no `caught_up` set), tests/external-review-launchers.test.sh:42 and :78 (stub `rebuild_publishes` / `worker_changed_files`), and the self rebuild suites through tests/lib/worker-rebuild.sh: tests/worker-rebuild.test.sh, tests/worker-rebuild-publication.test.sh and tests/spec-pin-sync.test.sh. Because those blocks run without the new variable, every new read of it is defaulted (`${caught_up:-0}`).

Callers and mirrors checked: `bring_up_to_date` is called only at bin/fm-worker.sh:1146; `rebuild_publishes` at :1826, :1828, :1866, :1883 and :1901; `rebuild_unresolved` from `rebuild_publishes`; `worker_changed_files` from `post_note` (:1655), the asked block (:1829, :1851, :1866, :1872, :1881, :1900), `worker_did_work`; `publish_wip_if_dirty` from the exit traps; `rebuild_refuse` only inside the pre-commit block; gate 2 only from `g 2` at bin/fm-gate.sh:268. Text mirrors: the message 'external rewrites require the explicit restack helper' appears only at bin/fm-worker.sh:1061 (grep bin/ tests/ design/ skills/); skills/firstmate/SKILL.md:1045 'External stacking/rebuild remains held for T-143.' is stale (T-143 merged in #154) and is rewritten in place to say an external later round merges its base in, never rebuilt or force-pushed, and gate 2 accepts a branch containing its base. bin/lib/fm-restack.sh and bin/lib/fm_stack.py (stacked PR restack) are not changed. bin/fm-checkpoint.sh's existing suite tests/worker-checkpoint.test.sh keeps passing (no merge in progress in any of its cases); the worker skill mirror is skills/worker/SKILL.md:98-119.

Design (edit in place, no new section at the end, T-189). design/design.md §5.3.3 'A later round starts from the current base' (design.md:930-1054) gains a paragraph after the rebuild description: an external project's branch is never rebuilt; its later round merges the fetched base into the branch (non-fast-forward merge, in progress until the round's commit), under the expected-head lease of the bound PR head, with conflicts handed to the worker as in a rebuild, the same refusals (exit 75), a clean catch-up always published, and a plain fast-forward push. §15.2 'Registry and conventions' (design.md:4836; the publication paragraph at design.md:4878-4884 that says 'T-143 enables policy-authorized stacking and explicit expected-head restacking') gains one sentence pointing to that paragraph, and in §6 'Lifecycle and the gates' (design.md:1101) the gate 2 row of the gates table (design.md:1207, '| 2 | rebase onto main is clean |') gains the external ancestor rule. The exit-code paragraph per the acceptance line above.

Migration / in flight: nothing stored changes format. agent-wardrobe T-002 (PR #1) is the first user: after T-223 merges, its next round (fm-worker --project maker-founder --task T-002) merges master in and hands main.cjs and styles.css to the worker. Self tasks in flight are unaffected (self path unchanged).
Out of scope: the self rebuild path's behaviour, the autopilot's update-branch, stacked-PR restacks, any change to external publication policy, landing or merge methods, and the board.
